experiments.title: Resistance of a wire as its length changes
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw the wire, test section, ammeter and voltmeter. Represent each chosen length by a resistance supplied from measurements or a declared wire model. Export V and I, calculate R, and plot R against length externally. Simulation cannot measure wire length or discover its material properties.

experiments.title: Equivalent resistance of series combinations
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare one, two and three resistors at a fixed supply. Record total current and calculate the equivalent resistance. Use separate saved circuits or a component-value study.

experiments.title: Equivalent resistance of parallel combinations
experiments.catalogue_description: Add branches and compare supply current with the individual branch currents. Show how adding a branch changes the effective load. Keep the numerical demand appropriate to GCSE; AQA does not require the parallel-resistance calculation itself.

experiments.title: I–V investigation: fixed resistor
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw the supply, current-limiting control, ammeter in series and voltmeter across the test resistor. Sweep supply voltage through positive and negative values. Export paired V/I readings for a characteristic graph and a resistance estimate.

experiments.title: I–V investigation: filament lamp
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw the same measurement circuit with a lamp. Compare measured data with an electrothermal or empirical lamp model. A fixed resistor with a lamp symbol will not reproduce the characteristic; a diagram and real laboratory measurements remain useful without that model.

experiments.title: I–V investigation: diode
experiments.catalogue_description: Use a diode model and series limiting resistor. Sweep the supply in both directions and measure voltage across the diode separately from supply voltage. Compare forward conduction and reverse current; use a graph scale that makes the intended feature visible.

experiments.title: Choosing and connecting electrical meters
experiments.catalogue_description: Prepare a resistor test circuit with correctly positioned instruments. Compare a resistance inferred from V/I with a resistance-mode reading on an unpowered circuit. Practise V Ω–COM for voltage/resistance and A–COM for current.

experiments.title: Current at different positions in one loop
experiments.catalogue_description: Put current probes before and after different components. Compare readings while changing supply voltage or resistance. Use a short transient capture to connect a steady current with charge transferred over a chosen time.

experiments.title: Voltage sharing in a series circuit
experiments.catalogue_description: Choose unequal resistors, measure each voltage and compare their sum with the supply. Swap the resistors and predict the new readings before running.

experiments.title: Branch current and voltage in parallel circuits
experiments.catalogue_description: Use two unequal branch resistors. Measure both branch voltages, both currents and the supply current. Repeat with one branch open.

experiments.title: Resistance of an NTC thermistor versus temperature
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw the measurement circuit and annotate the external temperature measurement. Enter measured R(T) values as separate runs, or supply a calibrated model. Plot resistance against temperature externally. A resistor-value sweep alone is not a temperature experiment.

experiments.title: Resistance of an LDR versus illumination
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw the LDR test circuit and label the controlled light conditions. Use measured resistance values for electrical predictions. TinyCAD does not model lamp distance, illumination or the LDR's optical response automatically.

experiments.title: Temperature-responsive sensor circuit
experiments.catalogue_description: Combine a thermistor-equivalent resistance with a fixed resistor and measure the output as the entered resistance changes. Compare the two sensor positions. This is a possible circuit for exploring the application; potential-divider calculations and a transistor/comparator switching stage are extensions, not additional GCSE requirements.

experiments.title: Light-responsive sensor circuit
experiments.catalogue_description: Repeat the sensor exercise with light/dark resistance values. Define whether the output should rise or fall as illumination decreases. A complete automatic lamp switch needs an additional switching model; changing resistance alone does not implement a switching threshold.

experiments.title: Resistor power and electrical energy
experiments.catalogue_description: Measure current and voltage for several resistor/supply combinations. Compare calculated power with a power trace; use a transient capture or a timed steady reading to calculate energy. This predicts electrical dissipation, not temperature rise or visible brightness.

experiments.title: Direct versus alternating voltage
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare a DC source with a low-voltage sine source on the scope. Identify polarity changes and repeat at different frequencies. This is an electronic demonstration of the distinction; it does not require a mains-voltage experiment.

experiments.title: LED polarity and a suitable series resistor
experiments.catalogue_description: Use an LED-specific model to compare current for different series resistors and supply polarities. This is a syllabus-linked diode application, not a separately required LED practical. Electrical current can be predicted; brightness, colour and damage are not automatically simulated.

experiments.title: Physical layout versus circuit diagram
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw a clear schematic from a photograph or bench arrangement, label meter connections and mark intended measurement points. Students can use it to construct or check the real experiment even when the lamp or sensor has no simulation model.

experiments.title: Wire resistivity
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw the wire test section and meters; annotate length and diameter measurements. Enter measured resistance values or a declared wire model. Use R versus length and the measured cross-sectional area to estimate resistivity externally. Simulation cannot supply independent evidence for the geometry or material law entered into it.

experiments.title: Cell emf and internal resistance
experiments.catalogue_description: Model a cell as an ideal voltage source with an explicit series resistor. Vary the load, collect terminal voltage and current, and fit V against I externally. Start with, for example, 1.5 V and 1 Ω; identify intercept and gradient. Do not confuse the bench supply's current limiting with a cell's internal resistance.

experiments.title: Capacitor charging
experiments.catalogue_description: Drive an RC circuit with a step and capture capacitor voltage and charging current. Vary R and C independently. Compare fitted or measured time constants and the time to reach a chosen fraction of the final voltage.

experiments.title: Capacitor discharging
experiments.catalogue_description: Capture decay after a known charging interval, using a suitable switch model or an explicitly stated source arrangement. Export the decay for a plot of ln(V) against time and obtain RC from its gradient. Include every discharge path, including meter resistance.

experiments.title: I–V characteristic of an ohmic resistor
experiments.catalogue_description: Sweep the source, collect component V and I and examine the gradient. Repeat with different resistance values; distinguish a V-against-I graph from an I-against-V graph.

experiments.title: I–V characteristic of a filament lamp
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare a measured characteristic with a validated lamp model. A constant resistance does not represent filament heating; without an electrothermal or empirical model, use TinyCAD for the experimental diagram.

experiments.title: I–V characteristic of a semiconductor diode
experiments.catalogue_description: Include current limiting, sweep both polarities and examine the diode's own voltage. Compare different valid diode models without assuming a universal fixed forward drop.

experiments.title: Thermistor resistance and a temperature-sensitive divider
experiments.catalogue_description: Enter measured temperature/resistance pairs or a calibrated sensor model. Compare output sensitivity over a chosen range. A generic resistor sweep explores circuit response but does not establish the temperature calibration.

experiments.title: Series/parallel networks and conservation checks
experiments.catalogue_description: Measure signed currents at a junction and voltage changes around a loop. Predict the effect of an extra branch or changed resistor, then compare numerical residuals.

experiments.title: Cells in series and identical cells in parallel
experiments.catalogue_description: Include an internal resistance for each source. Compare terminal voltage and load current for the same load; avoid modelling parallel cells as contradictory ideal voltage sources.

experiments.title: Adjustable potential divider
experiments.catalogue_description: Use two resistors, or two resistor segments representing a potentiometer. Vary the ratio and compare unloaded output with output connected to a finite load.

experiments.title: Light-dependent potential divider
experiments.catalogue_description: Substitute measured light/dark resistance values or a calibrated LDR model. Compare sensor positions and the resulting direction of output change. Illumination itself is external input data.

experiments.title: Electrical power and supply losses
experiments.catalogue_description: Measure delivered load power and power in an explicit source resistor. Vary the load and account for the electrical energy supplied. Physical cell heating and chemical behaviour need additional models.

experiments.title: Capacitance from transferred charge
experiments.catalogue_description: Integrate capacitor current over a selected interval and compare the resulting charge change with its voltage change. Repeat with different C values. Calculate the quotient externally if needed.

experiments.title: Plate spacing, area and dielectric: electrical measurement circuit
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw the capacitor and its measurement connections; annotate independently measured geometry and dielectric. The current multimeter has no capacitance range, and the circuit solver does not determine capacitance from drawn plate dimensions. Entering an assumed C only tests subsequent circuit behaviour.

experiments.title: Energy stored and dissipated in a capacitor circuit
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare calculated stored energy with the integral of discharge-resistor power. State the integration interval and initial voltage. A simulated discharge into a resistor is an electrical energy balance, not a temperature measurement.

experiments.title: Scope measurements of DC and sinusoidal signals
experiments.catalogue_description: Vary source amplitude, offset and frequency. Read volts/div and time/div, then compare cursor or graticule estimates with reported period and frequency. Use multiple cycles when estimating a period.

experiments.title: Sinusoidal peak, peak-to-peak and RMS measurements
experiments.catalogue_description: Capture complete cycles and compare a scope's voltage readout, AC meter reading and calculated RMS. Use a zero-offset sine initially; distinguish AC-only RMS from total RMS when adding an offset.

experiments.title: Meter loading and measurement error
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare a high-resistance divider with and without finite voltmeter input resistance. Compare current readings for different meter burdens. This is an evaluation exercise linked to the circuit topics, rather than another numbered required practical.

experiments.title: MOSFET transfer and output behaviour
experiments.catalogue_description: Use an N-channel enhancement device. Sweep gate voltage at several fixed drain conditions in separate runs, and measure drain current. Compare threshold estimates while keeping the model's limitations explicit.

experiments.title: MOSFET-controlled load
experiments.catalogue_description: Apply a pulse to the gate and compare gate, drain and load traces. Check the difference between an ideal switch assumption and a selected real device.

experiments.title: Zener characteristic and reference supply
experiments.catalogue_description: Sweep a limited supply through a series resistor, then test the reference with changed input and loading. Record diode voltage and current. Use a model containing the intended breakdown behaviour.

experiments.title: Photodiode detector circuit
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw the reverse-biased detector and readout. Use a calibrated photocurrent input to compare electrical response to steady and pulsed illumination. Wavelength response and optical intensity must come from external data/model parameters.

experiments.title: Hall-sensor interface and pulse readout
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw sensor supply, output and load. Use an equivalent voltage/pulse source to test the receiving electronics. Magnetic field and motion are not generated by the circuit solver.

experiments.title: Parallel LC response and damping
experiments.catalogue_description: Drive a parallel LC network through a stated source impedance. Sweep frequency, measure voltage gain and compare resonance with a calculated prediction. Change damping resistance and obtain bandwidth/Q. Use an energy-response or correctly squared voltage response for the syllabus's half-energy criterion.

experiments.title: Op-amp comparator
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare a varying sensor voltage with a reference. Observe the switching point and output limits. An unbounded ideal controlled source is not a realistic comparator; include suitable rail limiting or an amplifier model.

experiments.title: Inverting amplifier
experiments.catalogue_description: Choose two resistor ratios, apply a small sine and compare signed gain, phase and summing-node voltage. Repeat at larger input amplitude to expose saturation if the model supports it.

experiments.title: Non-inverting amplifier
experiments.catalogue_description: Repeat the gain measurement with a non-inverting configuration, then change the feedback ratio. Make supply rails and signal reference explicit in the diagram.

experiments.title: Summing amplifier
experiments.catalogue_description: Apply two independently adjustable inputs through different resistors. Compare the measured output with a weighted sum, then investigate clipping with a suitable model.

experiments.title: Difference amplifier
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare differential excitation with equal voltages on both inputs. Deliberately change one resistor to investigate imperfect common-mode rejection.

experiments.title: Amplifier frequency response
experiments.catalogue_description: Run small-signal AC analysis at several closed-loop gains. Measure cutoff/bandwidth and compare gain–bandwidth products. A frequency-independent ideal amplifier cannot demonstrate this behaviour.

experiments.title: Analogue signals and two-level regeneration
experiments.catalogue_description: Inject a known perturbation into a signal, then compare a threshold stage's input and output. Use explicit sources and a bounded comparator/gate model; investigate where the noise becomes too large to recover the intended levels.

experiments.title: Sampling, quantisation and PCM
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw an annotated sampler/ADC/encoding chain and identify where timing and voltage resolution enter. A working converter demonstration needs compatible mixed-signal models or external processing. Scope display sampling must not be described as an experiment on a modelled ADC.

experiments.title: Gate truth tables
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw gates, set all input combinations and compare output voltages with a truth table. Include AND, NAND, OR, NOR, NOT and EOR. Supply valid gate models and logic-level assumptions.

experiments.title: A logic network from a truth table
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw a proposed multi-gate network and test every input combination. Compare an alternative implementation of the same function. This can also be diagram-only work when models are unavailable.

experiments.title: Binary, BCD and Johnson counting
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw clock/reset connections and capture output sequences for each counter type. Test reset and, where applicable, counting direction. A prepared compatible counter model is required.

experiments.title: Modulo-n counter
experiments.catalogue_description: Add reset-decoding logic to a counter and verify the sequence length. Use a sufficiently small time step to capture reset pulses and avoid assuming ideal zero-delay behaviour.

experiments.title: Astable clock and duty cycle
experiments.catalogue_description: Use a suitable oscillator model, such as a modelled timer circuit. Vary its timing R/C and measure period, pulse width and duty cycle. Feeding in a predefined pulse source only supplies a clock; it does not test an astable. A specific timer IC is not required by this syllabus.

experiments.title: Electronic communication-chain connections
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw and annotate source, processing, transmitter, channel and receiver blocks. Identify which interfaces carry electrical signals. This is a block-diagram teaching exercise, not an end-to-end communication simulation.

experiments.title: Electrical model of a wired channel
experiments.catalogue_description: Represent a short wired connection by an explicitly justified R/C equivalent. Compare received pulses for different parameter sets. The model does not establish the behaviour of optical fibre or radio propagation.

experiments.title: Time-division multiplexing
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw two source channels, timed switches and a receiver arrangement. Annotate time slots. Simulation needs switch/control models and a prepared timing sequence; it is not a built-in multiplexing instrument.

experiments.title: AM waveform demonstration
experiments.catalogue_description: Supply a behavioural or compatible modulator model and compare carrier, message and modulated traces. Vary message amplitude/frequency. The proposed circuit implementation is optional; the syllabus does not require its details.

experiments.title: FM waveform demonstration
experiments.catalogue_description: Use the configurable source's FM waveform, then compare time-domain traces as modulation settings change. Identify carrier and message timing. A spectral sideband/bandwidth investigation requires external analysis or an added workflow; the current UI does not provide FFT.

experiments.title: Resistor combinations
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare series and parallel loads, predict supply current, and verify voltage sharing. Save a calculation alongside the circuit and numerical readings.

experiments.title: Adjustable sensor input
experiments.catalogue_description: Use a fixed resistor and variable sensor-equivalent resistance. Compare divider output over measured light or temperature conditions. The entered resistance is an assumption, not an optical or thermal simulation.

experiments.title: Push-button input and pull resistor
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw push-to-make and push-to-break arrangements. Use an explicit switch model or separate open/closed circuits to test the resulting input voltage.

experiments.title: LED output and current limiting
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare several limiting resistors and supplies using an LED model. Record current and resistor power; do not equate simulated current with measured brightness.

experiments.title: BJT switching stage
experiments.catalogue_description: Sweep the input to an NPN or PNP stage driving an electrical load. Compare input, output and device currents. Supply the correct model and pin mapping.

experiments.title: Darlington input stage
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare a single transistor with a pair for the same load. Investigate the input drive needed to reach a stated output condition.

experiments.title: FET switching stage
experiments.catalogue_description: Apply a gate-voltage sweep or pulse. Compare off/on output and load current using a chosen FET model.

experiments.title: Thyristor latch
experiments.catalogue_description: Apply a gate pulse and observe whether conduction persists after it ends. Model interruption of load current to reset the device. A transistor model is not an SCR substitute.

experiments.title: Threshold alarm
experiments.catalogue_description: Combine a sensor-equivalent input, comparator/transistor and LED load. Set a target threshold and compare predicted switching with measured sensor values. This is one possible implementation of the unit's design work.

experiments.title: RC timing stage
experiments.catalogue_description: Capture capacitor voltage after a source step. Change R and C separately and compare the measured delay to a chosen threshold.

experiments.title: Timer in monostable mode
experiments.catalogue_description: Use a compatible timer model, trigger once and measure pulse duration. Change the timing components. A predefined pulse source cannot demonstrate the timer's timing law.

experiments.title: Timer in astable mode
experiments.catalogue_description: Capture a timer's output and compare frequency/duty cycle for different component values. A flashing LED's electrical drive can be tested without modelling visual flashing.

experiments.title: Inductive-output protection
experiments.catalogue_description: Represent a relay coil by an explicit electrical model and compare switch-node voltage with and without a protection diode. Mechanical operation is outside the model.

experiments.title: Power-source suitability
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare the same circuit with an ideal source and a source having stated internal resistance. Battery chemistry and solar illumination need separate models or measurements.

experiments.title: PIC-based counter and display connections
experiments.catalogue_description: Document input switch, controller pins, supplies and display connections. Firmware execution, flowchart programming and seven-segment decoding are not ready-made TinyCAD workflows. Electrical interface stages can be tested separately.

experiments.title: Test-point and fault-diagnosis exercise
experiments.catalogue_description: Prepare a correct circuit and separate manually edited open/short/wrong-value versions. Predict diagnostic voltage/current readings. Record a test sequence for checking the physical build; this does not rely on an automatic fault-injection feature.

experiments.title: Construction and soldering preparation
experiments.catalogue_description: Produce a labelled schematic, polarity notes and a connectivity checklist for the physical assembly. TinyCAD does not turn the schematic into a breadboard photograph, demonstrate soldering competence or inspect joints.

experiments.title: Meter positions and loading
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare a divider with different voltmeter input resistances and current-meter burdens. Document which quantity each connection measures.

experiments.title: Potential-divider design
experiments.catalogue_description: Choose a target output and vary resistor ratio. Add a finite load and quantify the change rather than assuming an unloaded formula remains exact.

experiments.title: Emf and internal resistance
experiments.catalogue_description: Use an ideal source plus a series resistor. Change the load and fit terminal voltage against current using exported values. Identify the declared model's emf and resistance.

experiments.title: Ohmic/non-ohmic behaviour
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare resistor and LED characteristics using DC sweeps. Use a suitable electrothermal lamp model if including a filament lamp; a constant resistor cannot reproduce heating.

experiments.title: Capacitor reservoir and transferred charge
experiments.catalogue_description: Capture charge and discharge currents and capacitor voltage. Integrate current over a selected interval and compare with the voltage change.

experiments.title: Capacitors in series and parallel
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare networks using the same charging resistance. Infer equivalent capacitance from a transient response; the student multimeter has no capacitance range.

experiments.title: Capacitor filtering
experiments.catalogue_description: Apply a sine or pulse to an RC network. Compare input/output amplitude and timing across frequencies and relate the result to the chosen component values.

experiments.title: Peak and RMS readings
experiments.catalogue_description: Use a low-voltage sine source, scope and AC meter. Compare readings over complete cycles and distinguish a source's offset from its alternating component.

experiments.title: AC-to-DC supply stage
experiments.catalogue_description: Prepare a rectifier with compatible diodes and a smoothing capacitor. Vary load and capacitance; compare mean output and ripple from transient captures. This is an electronic implementation of the topic, not a complete mains-supply model.

experiments.title: LDR interface
experiments.catalogue_description: Enter measured sensor resistances for several illumination conditions and predict divider output. Optical distance/intensity must come from measurements or a declared model.

experiments.title: Thermistor interface
experiments.catalogue_description: Use measured R(T) values to compare output sensitivity and sensor placement. Keep the temperature calibration separate from the electrical prediction.

experiments.title: Strain-gauge bridge
experiments.catalogue_description: Model the bridge resistors and sweep a small declared resistance change. Measure differential output and the effect of an initially unbalanced bridge. Mechanical strain is not generated by the solver.

experiments.title: Reed-switch alarm interface
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw the switched input, bias resistor and indicator. Compare separate switch states or a compatible controlled switch. Magnetic actuation is external to the circuit.

experiments.title: Thermocouple readout and amplification
experiments.catalogue_description: Supply measured thermocouple voltages through a stated source resistance. Test loading and an amplifier interface. The model does not independently reproduce thermoelectric conversion.

experiments.title: Diode characteristic
experiments.catalogue_description: Use a limited DC sweep and collect component V/I. Compare selected signal and rectifier diode models, including the effect of the external resistor.

experiments.title: Half-wave rectification
experiments.catalogue_description: Capture a low-voltage sine input and resistive-load output. Compare polarity, conduction intervals and mean output.

experiments.title: Full-wave rectification
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw a bridge and identify which diodes conduct in each half-cycle. Compare output ripple frequency with the half-wave version.

experiments.title: Smoothing and load regulation
experiments.catalogue_description: Add a reservoir capacitor, change the load and capture ripple and mean voltage. Use transient analysis rather than a small-signal AC sweep to model rectifier conduction.

experiments.title: Zener reference/regulation
experiments.catalogue_description: Use a breakdown-capable model and a limiting resistor. Vary input and load, then compare output voltage, device current and power.

experiments.title: LED indicator design
experiments.catalogue_description: Select resistor values against a stated current target. Compare nominal and tolerance cases using the selected LED model. Brightness and damage require further modelling or measurement.

experiments.title: BJT switching
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare input drive, base current, collector current and output voltage through the switching range. Check a real model rather than imposing an unlimited current-gain assumption.

experiments.title: FET switching
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare electrical load response to gate pulses and input-voltage changes. Use the appropriate N/P-channel model and connections.

experiments.title: Transistor bias and operating point
experiments.catalogue_description: Adjust a bias network and inspect DC voltages/currents. Compare predicted and measured quiescent conditions before applying a signal.

experiments.title: Single-stage transistor amplifier
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare input/output amplitude and phase, then sweep frequency at a fixed bias. Obtain gain and bandwidth and repeat for a changed load.

experiments.title: Comparator threshold
experiments.catalogue_description: Sweep one input across a reference and capture output switching. Include supply limits and a suitable comparator/op-amp model.

experiments.title: Inverting amplifier
experiments.catalogue_description: Change feedback ratio, compare signed gain and inspect clipping with an adequately realistic model.

experiments.title: Non-inverting amplifier
experiments.catalogue_description: Repeat at several gains and compare input loading, output amplitude and operating range.

experiments.title: Amplifier/filter frequency response
experiments.catalogue_description: Supply a model with frequency dependence. Compare cutoff and gain–bandwidth behaviour; use a declared active filter topology if investigating its component sensitivity.

experiments.title: Gate truth tables
experiments.catalogue_description: Test all input combinations of the specified basic gates. State logic levels, supply and the selected device family.

experiments.title: TTL/CMOS interface and timing
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare loaded output and input thresholds using compatible models. Capture propagation delay only if the models represent it. Ideal Boolean behaviour cannot establish real-family specifications.

experiments.title: Minimise and verify combinational logic
experiments.catalogue_description: Prepare alternative implementations of a function and compare their complete truth tables. Karnaugh-map reasoning remains in the student's analysis, not an automatic TinyCAD tool.

experiments.title: Latches and flip-flops
experiments.catalogue_description: Apply defined clock/data/reset sequences to prepared R-S, D or JK models. Capture state changes and distinguish asynchronous inputs from clocked inputs.

experiments.title: Counters and shift register
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare three-stage counter or register sequences. Test reset and observe ripple delays where the model supports them.

experiments.title: Simulation-to-bench comparison
experiments.catalogue_description: Produce diagrams, saved settings, labelled results and a comparison table. Diagnose differences using measured components and instrument loading, then record the resulting design changes and personal reflection.

experiments.title: Physical build/test preparation
experiments.catalogue_description: Annotate supplies, polarity, pin names and test points. The schematic supports construction and measurement; it does not prove safe soldering, assembly quality or the learner's practical performance.

experiments.title: Nodal and loop checks
experiments.catalogue_description: Choose a multi-branch DC network, predict node potentials and signed currents, then compare simulation residuals with hand calculations.

experiments.title: Source superposition
experiments.catalogue_description: Solve a two-source circuit with each independent source deactivated in turn. Compare the sum of voltage/current contributions with the complete circuit. Do not sum power contributions as though power were linear.

experiments.title: Thevenin and Norton equivalents
experiments.catalogue_description: Obtain an equivalent at a selected port, then compare original and equivalent circuits under several finite loads. Avoid using a physical short as a measurement method.

experiments.title: Maximum power transfer
experiments.catalogue_description: Vary a resistor load against a source with explicit resistance. Compare load power and efficiency; maximum delivered power is not maximum efficiency.

experiments.title: Dividers and measurement loading
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare loaded/unloaded divider outputs and introduce finite meter input resistance. Quantify the measurement's influence.

experiments.title: Sinusoidal measurements
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare peak, RMS, frequency and phase using complete captured cycles. State whether an offset is included in the chosen RMS quantity.

experiments.title: RC and RL impedance
experiments.catalogue_description: Sweep frequency and compare the magnitude/phase of voltage and current with calculated impedances. Include source resistance and coil resistance where appropriate.

experiments.title: First-order transient response
experiments.catalogue_description: Capture RC and RL responses to a step. Change one component at a time and compare fitted time constants with the declared circuit.

experiments.title: RLC resonance and damping
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare time-domain decay with frequency response for different resistances. Measure resonance, bandwidth and Q using a stated criterion.

experiments.title: Passive filter response
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare RC low-pass/high-pass networks with the same source and load. Relate AC response to pulse-shape changes from transient runs.

experiments.title: Power factor in a small RLC load
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare average instantaneous power with apparent power calculated from RMS readings. Export values for complex-power calculations if required.

experiments.title: Half/full-wave rectification and smoothing
experiments.catalogue_description: Use low-voltage sources and explicit diode mappings. Vary load/capacitance and compare ripple and mean output. Treat transformer input as a declared source unless a suitable coupled model is supplied.

experiments.title: Diode and Zener behaviour
experiments.catalogue_description: Sweep current-limited circuits and compare operating voltage and dissipation. A Zener model must include the intended breakdown characteristic.

experiments.title: LED operating conditions
experiments.catalogue_description: Evaluate limiting resistors for several supplies using an identified LED model. Predict electrical current, not luminous intensity.

experiments.title: BJT switch and amplifier
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare switching and small-signal operation of a chosen transistor. Record DC bias before measuring gain and output range.

experiments.title: JFET/MOSFET comparison
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare gate-controlled current using appropriate models and separately stated operating conditions. Do not infer an interchangeable pinout or threshold.

experiments.title: Amplifier source/load interaction
experiments.catalogue_description: Vary source and load resistances around a prepared amplifier model. Measure gain and bandwidth under each condition.

experiments.title: Introductory op-amp feedback circuit
experiments.catalogue_description: Choose a simple inverting/non-inverting stage and compare predicted gain with captures. Supply rail limits and a model adequate to the measurement.

experiments.title: Voltage logic and simple gate networks
experiments.catalogue_description: Verify small combinational functions and state the logic-level conventions. Use appropriate gate models; neither firmware nor HDL execution is implied.

experiments.title: Signal-chain and test-plan drawing

experiments.title: DC network verification
experiments.catalogue_description: Solve a multi-loop network analytically, then compare signed currents and node voltages with the solver. Identify which discrepancies are numerical and which indicate a modelling or sign error.

experiments.title: Source resistance and loading
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare a measured source model with an ideal source while varying the load. Fit an equivalent source resistance from exported terminal readings.

experiments.title: Voltmeter loading
experiments.catalogue_description: Connect a finite-resistance meter to a high-resistance divider. Estimate the expected loading error before running, then compare with a physical meter.

experiments.title: Ammeter burden
experiments.catalogue_description: Repeat a low-resistance current measurement with several declared meter burdens. Quantify how inserting the instrument changes the circuit.

experiments.title: Capacitor combinations and energy
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare charging responses of series/parallel capacitor networks and calculate stored energy. Infer effective C using a stated method rather than a nonexistent virtual capacitance-meter range.

experiments.title: RC charging/discharging
experiments.catalogue_description: Capture both capacitor voltage and resistor current. Fit a decay externally, compare the time constant with component measurements and discuss instrument loading.

experiments.title: RL transient
experiments.catalogue_description: Apply a step to a resistive-inductive circuit, include coil resistance and compare fitted time constant with the model prediction. A lumped inductor does not model the magnetic geometry.

experiments.title: Damped RLC response
experiments.catalogue_description: Change R and compare oscillatory and non-oscillatory responses. Extract a decay rate and oscillation period from an adequately sampled transient.

experiments.title: Complex impedance and phase
experiments.catalogue_description: Sweep RC and RL circuits, measure voltage/current phase and compare with phasor calculations. State the reference direction and phase convention.

experiments.title: Series resonance
experiments.catalogue_description: Sweep an RLC circuit, measure response and bandwidth, then compare the inferred resonance with the transient experiment. Include generator output impedance.

experiments.title: AC power and power factor
experiments.catalogue_description: Average instantaneous load power and compare it with RMS-based apparent power. Calculate power factor and distinguish energy storage from dissipation.

experiments.title: Scope timing and amplitude measurements
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare graticule/cursor estimates with numerical readings as timebase and capture step change. Record the acquisition settings and avoid treating display interpolation as additional samples.

experiments.title: Transistor operating point and gain
experiments.catalogue_description: Bias a prepared BJT circuit, verify its DC state and compare small/large signal behaviour. Compare with a real circuit using an identified device.

experiments.title: Op-amp feedback and limits
experiments.catalogue_description: Test a simple amplifier at several gains and input amplitudes. Compare an idealised prediction with a rail-limited, frequency-dependent model and physical results.

experiments.title: Threshold detector and logic output
experiments.catalogue_description: Apply a slow input and a reference to a comparator, then check the resulting logic levels. The model must represent the required output limits.

experiments.title: Simple logic-network verification
experiments.catalogue_description: Prepare a small network, predict its truth table and exercise every combination. This is a proposed workshop exercise, not a claim that a particular gate exercise is allocated by Warwick.

experiments.title: Sensor calibration and interface loading
experiments.catalogue_description: Enter measured sensor voltage/resistance data and compare interface output for different loading. The physical calibration is obtained independently, not generated by fitting the same simulation.

experiments.title: Component uncertainty and model sensitivity
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare nominal and measured component values, then use bounded sweeps or tolerance studies. Keep manufacturing tolerances, instrument uncertainty and repeated-measurement scatter separate in the analysis.

experiments.title: Electronic measurement-chain documentation
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw sensor, conditioning stage, recorder/controller and references. Annotate supply and test connections. Firmware, physical data acquisition and weather-station operation need other tools.

experiments.title: Nodal and mesh analysis
experiments.catalogue_description: Solve the same network by two analytical methods and compare each node/current with the numerical solution. Use signed reference arrows.

experiments.title: Source superposition
experiments.catalogue_description: Run separate single-source conditions and the full circuit. Compare voltages/currents, and explain why powers cannot simply be superposed.

experiments.title: Thevenin/Norton models
experiments.catalogue_description: Derive a port equivalent and compare original/equivalent circuits across a load sweep. Record port definitions and reference direction.

experiments.title: Sources, loads and power
experiments.catalogue_description: Vary a finite load against explicit source resistance. Compare delivered power and internal dissipation without assuming that maximum power means maximum efficiency.

experiments.title: Meter loading and generator impedance
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare theoretical unloaded values with the actual virtual instruments attached. Include function-generator output resistance and meter burden/input resistance.

experiments.title: RC/RL complete step response
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare initial condition, forced response and final state. Choose capture duration and step from the fastest/slowest relevant time constants.

experiments.title: Impedance and phase
experiments.catalogue_description: Sweep frequency and calculate complex impedance from voltage/current results. Compare magnitude and phase with the analytical prediction.

experiments.title: Resonant network
experiments.catalogue_description: Use a declared RLC topology and vary damping. Compare frequency response with its transient ringing and measure the relevant bandwidth.

experiments.title: Passive filters
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare low/high-pass response using AC analysis, then apply pulses in transient analysis. Explain the effect of loading on the nominal cutoff.

experiments.title: Energy storage and loss
experiments.catalogue_description: Integrate current or component power over a stated interval. Check the energy balance for a capacitor or inductor network against analytical calculations.

experiments.title: Diode characteristic and operating point
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare a chosen SPICE diode with an ideal/piecewise analytical approximation. Examine where the approximation produces an unacceptable error.

experiments.title: Rectification and smoothing
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare half/full-wave circuits and load-dependent ripple with a low-voltage sine source. Include real diode models and use transient analysis.

experiments.title: Transistor bias and load line
experiments.catalogue_description: Predict DC operating point, run the model and repeat for component tolerances. Export device readings for a load-line comparison.

experiments.title: BJT amplifier gain and resistance
experiments.catalogue_description: Measure small-signal gain and infer input/output resistance using controlled source/load changes. Compare with a small-signal equivalent.

experiments.title: FET characteristics and switching
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare selected gate/drain conditions with a device model. Investigate gate-drive and load effects rather than assuming every FET is an ideal switch.

experiments.title: Op-amp feedback stages
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare inverting and non-inverting gain, input loading and output range. Distinguish an ideal analytical block from a model with rails and frequency limits.

experiments.title: Active filter
experiments.catalogue_description: Measure a prepared op-amp filter's gain/phase and pulse response. Compare component changes with the predicted poles/cutoff using an appropriate amplifier model.

experiments.title: Logic functions and minimisation
experiments.catalogue_description: Test a truth table against two alternative gate implementations. Do the Boolean/Karnaugh-map reasoning separately and compare all input combinations.

experiments.title: Multiplexer, decoder and encoder
experiments.catalogue_description: Use compatible component models or a gate-level circuit. Capture outputs while enumerating data/select inputs.

experiments.title: Latch versus edge-triggered flip-flop
experiments.catalogue_description: Apply a defined clock/data sequence and compare stored state. State timing assumptions; ideal models do not establish real setup/hold limits.

experiments.title: Counter and shift register
experiments.catalogue_description: Verify reset and output sequences and compare synchronous/asynchronous operation where delay models permit.

experiments.title: Logic-family loading and propagation
experiments.catalogue_description: Vary capacitance/fan-out within a valid device model. Measure edge and propagation timing. A zero-delay Boolean model is insufficient.

experiments.title: Adder and overflow indication
experiments.catalogue_description: Implement a small gate-level arithmetic example and enumerate operand combinations. Explain signed/unsigned interpretation outside the circuit.

experiments.title: State-machine I/O plan
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw the input/output, clock/reset and state-register interfaces for a small controller. A separate HDL tool is needed to implement, synthesise and verify SystemVerilog.

experiments.title: FPGA/microcontroller interface schematic
experiments.catalogue_description: Record supplies, connectors, pull resistors and external driver stages. TinyCAD does not program an FPGA, execute firmware or replace the course's digital development environment.

experiments.title: Integrated design/test exercise
experiments.catalogue_description: Combine a defined input, conditioner and output stage. Save analytical targets, model identities, captures, loading assumptions and a plan for bench comparison. The project brief is our proposal, not an institution-prescribed assignment.

experiments.title: Instrument connections and measurement loading
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare a divider's predicted output with finite-resistance voltage measurement and compare current readings with stated burden. Explain how an instrument changes the circuit.

experiments.title: DC network analysis
experiments.catalogue_description: Use a multi-branch resistor circuit and compare measured node/current values with nodal and mesh calculations.

experiments.title: Equivalent source and load
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare an original network with its port equivalent for several loads. State source resistance and avoid treating an ideal source as a complete battery model.

experiments.title: Superposition
experiments.catalogue_description: Investigate each independent source separately, then compare the total voltage/current. Show explicitly why power is not a linear sum of these separate results.

experiments.title: Electrical power budget
experiments.catalogue_description: Account for resistor, source and load power for different operating conditions. Distinguish predicted electrical dissipation from temperature rise or mechanical output.

experiments.title: RC step response
experiments.catalogue_description: Capture voltage/current, measure time constant and compare loading assumptions. Repeat with measured component values.

experiments.title: RL response and coil resistance
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare current rise for an idealised and resistive coil model. The experiment concerns its electrical terminals, not magnetic geometry or motion.

experiments.title: Damped RLC response
experiments.catalogue_description: Change resistance and compare transient oscillation/decay and frequency response. Choose sampling and run length from the expected response.

experiments.title: Impedance and phase
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare an RC/RL load's frequency-dependent current with phasor calculations. Keep phase reference and current direction explicit.

experiments.title: AC power and power factor
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare average instantaneous power with RMS-derived apparent power for a small circuit model. Complete complex-power calculations externally if necessary.

experiments.title: Passive filter and pulse distortion
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare frequency response and transient response of the same RC filter under defined source/load conditions.

experiments.title: Diode and rectifier interface
experiments.catalogue_description: Use current limiting, an identified diode model and low-voltage sine input. Compare polarity, conduction and output ripple. The rectifier topology is a proposed application of the device topic.

experiments.title: Transistor load driver
experiments.catalogue_description: Investigate drive voltage/current and output loading using a prepared transistor model. For an inductive equivalent load, compare switch-node voltage with protection included.

experiments.title: Op-amp conditioner
experiments.catalogue_description: Scale a declared low-level input to a desired output range. Compare loading, gain and saturation with a suitable amplifier model.

experiments.title: Active filter
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare the passive and buffered/active versions of a selected filter under changed loading. Use a model with adequate bandwidth.

experiments.title: Logic decision circuit
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw a small combinational controller and verify all combinations against a stated truth table. Compatible gate models are required; programming an industrial controller is separate.

experiments.title: Sensor-to-controller interface
experiments.catalogue_description: Supply measured sensor voltages/resistances and investigate offset, loading and conditioning. Do not claim the circuit independently reproduces the physical sensing mechanism.

experiments.title: System connections and test plan
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw supplies, references, sensor connections, driver and receiving equipment, with test points. The full mechanical/process/software system remains outside TinyCAD.
